questions.prompt: 1. Choose the phrase that best completes the sentence: “After I have breakfast, I _____ in the bathroom before I go to school.”
questions.evidence: “Brush my teeth” is the morning bathroom routine before going to school; “set the table” and “cook dinner” are mealtime actions.

questions.prompt: 2. Which daily routine phrase means putting your school books into your bag for the next day?
questions.evidence: “Pack a bag” means putting school books and supplies into your bag; “make the bed” is tidying bedcovers and “get dressed” is putting on clothes.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Places and jobs vocabulary
questions.prompt: 3. Choose the place word from the lesson that completes the sentence: “Sami works in a _____. Every day, he takes care of sick people there.”
questions.evidence: A hospital is the workplace where doctors and nurses take care of sick people.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Telling the time (past, to, quarter, half)
questions.prompt: 4. Look at the digital clock below. How do we say 7:15 in English?
questions.evidence: Fifteen minutes after seven (7:15) is “quarter past seven”. (“Quarter to seven” is 6:45, and “half past seven” is 7:30.)

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Telling the time (past, to, quarter, half)
questions.prompt: 5. Our English lesson starts at ten to nine. Which digital time matches “ten to nine”?
questions.evidence: “Ten to nine” means ten minutes before nine o’clock, which is 8:50. (9:10 is “ten past nine”.)

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Telling the time (past, to, quarter, half)
questions.prompt: 6. Rami has lunch at 2:30 in the afternoon. Choose the sentence that gives the same time.
options: a) Rami has lunch at twenty-five past two.
b) Rami has lunch at half past two.
c) Rami has lunch at quarter to three.
questions.evidence: Thirty minutes after two o’clock (2:30) is “half past two”.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, sometimes, never)
questions.prompt: 7. Choose the correct frequency adverb: “Nadia goes to school on foot every school day. She _____ goes to school by bus.”
questions.evidence: Because Nadia walks to school on foot every school day, she goes by bus on zero days, so “never” is the only accurate adverb.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a five-day routine schedule with frequency adverbs
questions.prompt: 8. Look at Mazen’s five-day table below. Which sentence matches the table?
options: b) Mazen usually reads a book.
c) Mazen sometimes brushes his teeth.
questions.evidence: In Mazen’s table, “read a book” has ticks on four of the five days (Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri) and one cross, which matches “usually”.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a five-day routine schedule with frequency adverbs
questions.prompt: 9. Look at Mazen’s table below and choose True or False: “Mazen sometimes plays computer games.”
questions.evidence: The “play computer games” row has a cross (×) on all five days, so Mazen never plays computer games and the statement is False.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Present simple affirmative (-s / -es / has)
questions.prompt: 10. Choose the correct verb form: “Kareem always _____ his homework in his bedroom before dinner.”
questions.evidence: “Kareem” is third-person singular (he), and verbs ending in -o add -es in the present simple: do → does.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Present simple negatives (don’t / doesn’t)
questions.prompt: 11. Choose the grammatically correct negative sentence:
options: a) Fadi doesn’t go to work on Fridays.
b) Fadi don’t go to work on Fridays.
c) Fadi doesn’t goes to work on Fridays.
questions.evidence: With “Fadi” (he), the present simple negative uses “doesn’t” followed by the plain base verb “go” without -es.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Present simple questions (Do / Does)
questions.prompt: 12. Complete the question: “_____ your cousins study together in the afternoon?”
questions.evidence: “Your cousins” is plural (they) and “study” is a base verb, so the present simple question begins with “Do”.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading comprehension of a daily routine text
questions.prompt: 13. Read Bilal’s routine below and choose True or False: “Bilal and Ziad make their beds before they go to school.”
questions.evidence: The passage states: “First, we make our beds and have breakfast with our parents. Then we go to school on foot at half past seven.”

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading comprehension of a daily routine text
questions.prompt: 14. Read Bilal’s routine below. Who usually tidies his bedroom in the afternoon?
questions.evidence: The passage states: “In the afternoon, Ziad usually tidies his bedroom”.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading comprehension of a daily routine text
questions.prompt: 15. Read Bilal’s routine below. What time do Bilal and Ziad get up on school days?
questions.evidence: The second sentence states: “On school days, my brother Ziad and I get up at quarter to seven.”

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking and answering about daily routine times
questions.prompt: 16. Choose the best reply to complete this conversation: “What time does your mother go to work?”
options: a) Yes, she goes to work.
b) She goes to work at quarter past eight.
c) She works in a hospital.
questions.evidence: “What time does …?” asks for a clock time, so “She goes to work at quarter past eight.” answers the question directly and grammatically.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Editing third-person singular verbs (-s / -es)
questions.prompt: 17. Correct the underlined verb mistake in this sentence. Write one word only:
questions.evidence: “Adel” is third-person singular (he), and “go” ends in -o, so it takes -es in the present simple: goes.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing present simple questions in the right word order
questions.prompt: 18. Put all five words in the right order to write a present simple question:
questions.evidence: A present simple question with “Maysa” (she) begins with “Does”, followed by the subject “Maysa”, the plain verb “tidy”, and the object “her bedroom”: “Does Maysa tidy her bedroom?”
